hypotheses.justification: The conclusion quantifies over all V with (∀ x, ‖V x‖ ≤ B). Any such V gives 0 ≤ ‖V 0‖ ≤ B, so 0 ≤ B follows from hV once V is introduced. If B < 0 no V exists and the statement holds vacuously. The proof changes only slightly. U₀ is built from C, ε and the tendsto statement, and none of that uses hB. After `intro ... hV ...`, put `have hB : 0 ≤ B := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hV 0)` before calling `terminalRemainder_tsum_bound`. This hypothesis can be deleted on its own, and also together with hBT.

This is the same argument as for hB. The conclusion has (∀ x, ‖T x‖ ≤ BT) as a hypothesis on T, so 0 ≤ BT follows from `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hT 0)`. If BT < 0, no T exists and the statement is vacuous. The constant C and the tendsto step do not use hBT. It is only used as an argument to terminalRemainder_tsum_bound, which can be given the derived fact instead. This hypothesis can be deleted on its own, and also together with hB.
